claim: For rooted full binary trees with unit-length edges, the variance \(V_T(k)\) of rooted phylogenetic diversity under uniform \(k\)-leaf rarefaction is unimodal for every tree with \(1\le n\le9\) leaves, and this cutoff is sharp: the 10-leaf tree whose root children are a perfect balanced 8-leaf subtree and a 2-leaf cherry has \(V_T(1),\ldots,V_T(10)=(16/25,136/225,28/45,1306/2205,1916/3969,3884/11025,2/9,8/81,0,0)\), with \(V_T(1)>V_T(2)<V_T(3)>V_T(4)\), so its variance curve is not unimodal.
integrity: Exact rational arithmetic; exhaustive finite census of rooted plane full binary shapes through nine leaves and all subsets; witness checked by direct enumeration and the clade-covariance formula.
scientific_limitations: Only rooted full binary trees with unit-length edges and uniform fixed-size leaf subsets without replacement; no claim for unequal branch lengths, multifurcating trees, unrooted PD, sampling with replacement, or empirical communities.
title: The sharp ten-leaf boundary for non-unimodal rooted phylogenetic-diversity variance under rarefaction
